ALSO, DURING THIS INCIDENT ALL OTHER RIGHT ENGINE INDICATORS STAYED NORMAL/IN THE GREEN. AFTER THIS WE ATTEMPTED TO LEAVE RVSM AIRSPACE, BUT ON DESCENT THE PRIMARY AIRSPEED INDICATOR DISPLAYED US SLOWING DOWN. WE THEN REALIZED ADC1 WAS ACTUALLY THE WRONG ADC AND REVERTED TO ADC2 WHICH WORKED PROPERLY, HOWEVER WE WERE UNABLE TO REENGAGE YD OR AP.  CONTINUING OUR DESCENT WE RECEIVED A HDG AND ATT FLAG WHICH DISABLED OUR FLIGHT DIRECTOR. WE BRIEFLY SWITCHED TO STANDBY INDICATORS AND NOTICED THAT AHRS1 WAS SHOWING US PITCHED UP 10 DEGREES DESPITE BEING IN A DESCENT. WE THEN REVERTED TO AHRS2 AND DECIDED TO DIVERT TO ICT IN ORDER TO DETERMINE THE MECHANICAL FAULT.  ON THE WAY TO ICT ATC DECLARED AN EMERGENCY ON OUR BEHALF AND GAVE US PRIORITY HANDLING TO THE RUNWAY. WE RECEIVED VECTORS TO THE AIRPORT TO ENSURE WE WERE HEADED THE RIGHT WAY AND LANDED AT ICT USING VISUAL INDICATIONS.

HAD 2 GREENS FOR MAINS AND A NEGATIVE INDICATION FOR THE MECHANICAL NOSE INDICATOR. NO ANNUNCIATOR FOR HYDRAULICS. JUST RED FOR NOSE GEAR. ASKED FO TO CYCLE GEAR UP THEN BACK DOWN. SAME RESULT: TWO GREENS AND RED ON NOSE. WANTED A VISUAL ON THE GEAR IF WE COULD GET IT AND ASKED TOWER FOR A LOW PASS AND IF THEY WOULD VISUALLY VERIFY COCKPIT INDICATIONS. TOWER INFORMED US TWO MAINS DOWN WITH NO NOSEWHEEL AND DOORS SHUT. ASKED TOWER FOR DELAY VECTORS TO WORK ON THE PROBLEM. FO GOT OUT THE CHECKLIST AND WE STARTED PROCEDURE ACCORDING TO THE CHECKLIST. THE TOWER INFORMED US THEY WERE DECLARING AN EMERGENCY WHEN WE ASKED FOR THE VISUAL FOR THE LONGER RUNWAY. WE PINNED THE PLANE AND SHUT IT DOWN.

DURING ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS WHILE PROCESSING OF A CUSTOMER COMPLAINT (202502-1029217) MTU MAINTENANCE  CHECKED PREVIOUSLY REPAIRED GE90 FAN STATOR MODULES INCLUDING MODULES REPAIRED BY OTHER REPAIR STATIONS AND FOUND A DIFFERENCE IN THE APPLIED POLYSULFIDE MATERIAL ADJACENT TO THE FAN ABRADABLE AREA.  MTU WORKING DOCUMENTATION WAS SUBSEQUENTLY REVIEWED AND DID NOT REFLECT APPLICATION OF POLYSULFIDE IN THIS AREA. MTU REVIEWED THE TECHNICAL DATA TO IDENTIFY, WHY THE MATERIAL WAS USED IN THIS AREA. IT WAS SUSPECTED, THAT THE UNKNOWN POLYSULPHITE APPLICATION WAS RELATED TO A DIFFERENT INTERPRETATION OF EM CHAPTER 72-00-24 REPAIR 003 (REPLACEMENT OF DAMAGED SEALS AND REPAIR OF AXIAL AND CIRCUMFERENTIAL CLOSEOUTS). TO VERIFY THIS SUSPICION AND IDENTIFY THE CORRECT PROCEDURE MTU CONTACTED THE OEM AND OPENED CASE NO. #02135752. THE OEM STATED, THAT THE USE OF POLYSULFIDE IN THIS AREA IS CORRECT FOR REPAIR 003  REQUIRES THE APPLICATION OF POLYSULFIDE TO THE CLOSEOUT AREAS.  BASED ON THIS INFORMATION MTU INVESTIGATED ON THE WORK ORDERS ALREADY PERFORMED AND IDENTIFIED, THAT ON THE PARTS LISTED IN ATTACHMENT 1 MTU DID NOT APPLY POLYSULFIDE IN THE SPLIT LINE AREA AS REQUESTED PER EM 72-00-24 REPAIR 003. FOLLOWING STEPS OF 72-00-24 REPAIR 003 HAVE NOT BEEN PERFORMED:  REPLACEMENT OF THE FIBERGLASS WITH POLYSULFIDE UNDER THE ABRADABLE INADVERTANTLY NOT PERFORMED, REFER TO SUBTASK 72-00-24-300-004 AND 72-24-01-350-129.   REPLACEMENT OF THE FIBERGLASS WITH POLYSULFIDE IN THE VERTICAL PART UP TO THE FAN CASE INADVERTANTLY NOT PERFORMED, REFER TO SUBTASK 72-24-01-350-117 AND SUBTASK 72-00-24-300-004. FROM OUR INTERNAL RISK ASSESSMENT, MTU CONSIDERS THE MENTIONED MISSING STEPS AS NOT FLIGHT SAFETY RELEVANT, REQUIRING NO IMMEDIATE ACTIONS. THE RISK, THAT WAS IDENTIFIED, IS PRIMARILY, THAT THE MOISTURE CAN GET THROUGH THE GAP BETWEEN TWO ADJACENT TRENCH FILLERS, AND THE MOISTURE MIGHT LEAD TO CORROSION. THIS CORROSION CAN POTENTIALLY LEAD TO UN-SERVICEABLITY OF THE PART AT THE NEXT SHOP INSPECTION, BUT NO ULTIMATE FAILURE OF THE PART, WHICH WOULD LEAD TO A SAFETY RELEVANT EVENT. FURTHERMORE FOR ALL IN SHOP HANDLED FAN STATOR MODULES, NO FINDINGS IN THE FIBERGLASS CLOSEOUTS WERE IDENTIFIED, WHICH WOULD MAKE A REPAIR MANDATORY. THE APPLICATION OF POLYSULFIDE AS PART OF REPAIR 003 IS A PROACTIVE MEASURE TO PREVENT FUTURE ENTRY OF MOISTURE IN THE SPLIT LINE. MTU SHOP HANDLING GUIDE WORKSCOPE LEVEL TSO1 REQUIRED REPAIR 003 AS THIS PROACTIVE MEASURE. MTU CONTACTED THE OEM FOR TECHNICAL SUPPORT AND TO CONFIRM THE RISK ASSESSMENT AS WELL AS TERMINATING ACTIONS SUGGESTED BY MTU, REFER TO CASE #02144932. AIRCRAFT WAS IN MAINTENANCE TO HAVE THE MAIN LANDING GEAR INSPECTED DUE TO PRIOR ISSUES NOTED ON OUR OTHER AIRCRAFT. PER OUR REQUEST, AIRCRAFT WAS PLACED ON JACKS AND THE LANDING GEAR WAS CYCLED TO SEE IF THERE WERE ANY ISSUES, IE; BINDING OR NOISES COMING FROM THE MAIN LANDING GEAR TRUNNIONS WHILE GEAR WAS BEING EXTENDED AND RE-TRACKED. TEXTRON AVIATION ORLANDO SERVICE CENTER MAINTENANCE TECHNICIANS NOTED THAT BOTH MAIN LANDING GEAR FORWARD TRUNNION PIVOT BEARINGS APPEARED TO BE SEIZED, WHICH IS CAUSING RESISTANCE/BINDING AND NOISE WHEN RETRACTING AND EXTENDING THE MAIN LANDING GEAR. MAINTENANCE CREWS ATTEMPTED TO GREASE THESE TWO FORWARD TRUNNION BEARINGS, HOWEVER ONLY ONE SIDE INITIALLY WOULD ACCEPT GREASE. AFTER SOME EFFORT, THE SECOND SIDE STARTED ACCEPTING GREASE. ONCE BOTH MAIN LANDING GEAR FORWARD PIVOT BEARINGS WERE GREASED, THE NOISE AND BINDING OF THE TRUNNIONS DECREASED WHEN CYCLING THE GEAR. IT WAS  THE ORLANDO SERVICE CENTER THEN REMOVED BOTH MAIN LANDING GEAR TRUNNION ASSEMBLIES FROM THE AIRCRAFT TO INSPECT THE FORWARD PIVOT BEARINGS AND PIVOT PINS. AFTER REMOVAL OF BOTH TRUNNIONS, THE LEFT FORWARD BEARING/PIVOT PIN WERE SEIZED TOGETHER. AND AFTER SEVERAL HOURS, THE OLD PIN AND PIVOT BEARING WERE REMOVED. THE MAIN LANDING GEAR ASSEMBLIES WERE REINSTALLED WITH NEW FORWARD TRUNNION PIVOT BEARING AND PIVOT PINS. NOTE: LUBRICATION INTERVAL PER THE TEXTRON AVIATION 525C MM FOR THIS BEARING IS ONCE EVERY 12 MONTHS, THIS AIRCRAFT IS APPROXIMATELY 8 MONTHS OLD.

MARCH 19, 2025, A CESSNA S550 SUFFERED AN UN-COMMANDED NOSE LANDING GEAR (NLG) RETRACTION EVENT WHEN LANDING. AN INQUIRY OF THE NTSB AND FAA DATABASES FOR UN-COMMANDED GEAR EVENTS ON CESSNA 500 SERIES JET AIRCRAFT REVEALED MULTIPLE HITS. IN THE YEARS OF 2001, 2009, 2012 AND 2020, SIMILAR, IF NOT EXACT OCCURRENCES OF UN-COMMANDED GEAR RETRACTIONS DURING LANDING SEQUENCE HAVE BEEN INVESTIGATED BY THE NTSB AND UNITED KINGDOM’S AIR ACCIDENTS INVESTIGATION BRANCH (AAIB). -	RESEARCH INTO CESSNA 550 LANDING GEAR SYSTEMS REVEALED SERVICE BULLETIN (SB)  550-32-54, LANDING GEAR – NLG ACTUATOR REPLACEMENT (DATED NOV 26, 2008).WHEN ATTEMPTING TO DOWNLOAD THIS SB ON TEXTRON CESSNA’S WEBSITE, IT DID NOT SHOW AS AVAILABLE. CESSNA “TEAM LEGACY” ENGINEERS WERE CONTACTED AND PRODUCED THE SERVICE BULLETIN. THE SB IS DOCUMENTED BY CESSNA AS, ‘MANDATORY – MUST BE ACCOMPLISHED DURING THE NEXT PHASE 2 INSPECTION AND OR NOT TO EXCEED 24 MONTHS.’ THE SB REQUIRES UPGRADING INSTALLED NLG ACTUATORS FROM P/N 9912120-2 TO 9912120-4. SUBJECT ACTUATORS INCORPORATE AN INTERNAL LOCK TO HOLD THE GEAR IN THE EXTENDED POSITION. THE -4 INCORPORATES AN IMPROVED INTERNAL LOCKING MECHANISM DESIGN. AN AIRFRAME MOUNTED UPLOCK, LOCATED IN THE NOSE WHEEL WELL, HOLDS THE NLG RETRACTED DURING FLIGHT. THE SERVICE BULLETIN SHOWS AN EFFECTIVITY FOR MODEL 550 (CITATION II), SERIAL NUMBERS -0727 THRU -0733. THE INCIDENT AIRCRAFT IS S/N 0072 WHICH DOES NOT FALL INTO THE SB APPLICABILITY RANGE. THIS IS WHY, DURING SB SEARCH, THE SB DID NOT SHOW UP AS S/N FILTERS PREVENTED VISIBILITY. THE NLG ACTUATOR MANUFACTURER, NABTESCO AEROSPACE (FORMALLY TEIJIN SEIKI AEROSPACE) WAS CONTACTED TO CLARIFY THE DIFFERENCES IN P/NS AND WHY THE NEED FOR A P/N CHANGE WAS NECESSARY. THEIR REPLY; “THE DESIRE TO IMPROVE WEAR LIFE AND LOCKING MECHANISM DESIGN”. A REVIEW OF THE AIRCRAFT’S MAINTENANCE LOGBOOK ENTRIES REVEALED THE NLG ACTUATOR WAS REMOVED AND REPLACED ON JUNE 22, 2005. AN OVERHAULED ACTUATOR WAS INSTALLED, P/N: 9912120-2, S/N: 1054. THE REMOVED ACTUATOR OF THE SAME P/N, S/N 624, WAS DOCUMENTED WITH THE DISCREPANCY “WORN TO LIMITS”. WITH P/N 9912120-2 INSTALLED, SB 550-32-54 NOW BECOMES APPLICABLE EVEN THOUGH THE AIRCRAFT S/N FALLS OUTSIDE THE EFFECTIVITY RANGE MENTIONED EARLIER. THE SB HAS A TWO YEAR WINDOW FOR COMPLIANCE. THIS MEANS THE INCIDENT AIRCRAFT’S NLG ACTUATOR WAS REQUIRED TO BE UPGRADED NO LATER THAN NOV 2010 (TWO YEARS AFTER SB RELEASE). AS OF 2025, THE INCIDENT AIRCRAFT’S INSTALLED ACTUATOR IS ROUGHLY 15 YEARS OVERDUE SB COMPLIANCE. MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL DID NOT HAVE VISIBILITY TO RECOGNIZE THIS OVERDUE SITUATION AS THE SB DOES NOT INCLUDE THE INCIDENT AIRCRAFT’S S/N IN THE EFFECTIVITY FIELD. INVESTIGATION HAS DETERMINED THE PROBABLE CAUSE(S) OF THIS INCIDENT TO BE: DISENGAGEMENT OF THE NLG ACTUATOR’S INTERNAL LOCK FOR UNKNOWN REASONS RESULTING IN AN UN-COMMANDED RETRACTION OF THE NLG ACTUATOR PISTON. RECOMMENDATIONS FOR TEXTRON CESSNA: AMEND SERVICE BULLETIN 550-32-54 TO INCLUDE ALL 550 AIRCRAFT SERIAL NUMBERS. CURRENT APPLICABILITY IS LIMITED ONLY TO AIRCRAFT WITH SERIAL NUMBERS -0727 THRU -733. CESSNA SHOULD CONSIDER THAT AIRCRAFT WITH SERIAL NUMBERS WHICH FALL OUTSIDE OF THIS RANGE, MAY HAVE UNMODIFIED ACTUATOR P/N: 9912120-2 INSTALLED. THIS MAKES THE SB APPLICABLE, SUCH AS IN THE CASE OF THE INCIDENT AIRCRAFT. RECOMMEND SB BE AMENDED TO READ: “APPLICABILITY - ANY 550 AIRCRAFT WITH INSTALLED NLG ACTUATOR PART NUMBERS OTHER THAN 9912120-4”. WHILE SB 550-32-54 IS BEING AMENDED, ISSUE A ONE-TIME INSPECTION OF NLG ACTUATORS ON 550 AIRCRAFT, SERIAL NUMBERS -0002 THRU 0726. THIS INSPECTION WILL IDENTIFY AIRCRAFT WHICH DID NOT ORIGINALLY FALL WITHIN THE SB EFFECTIVITY RANGE BUT MAY HAVE UNMODIFIED ACTUATORS IN NEED OF SB COMPLIANCE SUCH AS IN THE CASE OF THE INCIDENT AIRCRAFT.

DURING ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS WHILE PROCESSING OF A CUSTOMER COMPLAINT (202502-1029217) MTU MAINTENANCE HANNOVER GMBH CHECKED PREVIOUSLY REPAIRED GE90 FAN STATOR MODULES INCLUDING MODULES REPAIRED BY OTHER REPAIR STATIONS FOR COMPARISON AND FOUND A DIFFERENCE IN THE APPLIED POLYSULFIDE MATERIAL BELOW THE FAN ABRADABLE AREA AS WELL AS THE RADIAL PORTION OF THE CLOSEOUT.  MTU WORKING DOCUMENTATION WAS SUBSEQUENTLY REVIEWED AND DID NOT REFLECT APPLICATION OF POLYSULFIDE IN THIS AREA.  MTU REVIEWED THE TECHNICAL DATA TO IDENTIFY, WHY THE MATERIAL WAS USED IN THIS AREA.  IT WAS SUSPECTED, THAT THE UNKNOWN POLYSULFIDE APPLICATION WAS RELATED TO A DIFFERENT INTERPRETATION OF EM CHAPTER 72-00-24 REPAIR 003 (REPLACEMENT OF DAMAGED SEALS AND REPAIR OF AXIAL AND CIRCUMFERENTIAL CLOSEOUTS) AND 7 2-24-01 REPAIR 013 (TRENCH FILLER AND CLOSEOUT REPAIR). TO VERIFY THIS SUSPICION AND IDENTIFY THE CORRECT PROCEDURE MTU CONTACTED THE OEM AND OPENED CASE NO. #02135752 AND #02135634. THE OEM STATED, THAT THE USE OF POLYSULFIDE IN THIS AREA IS CORRECT FOR BOTH REPAIRS 003 AND 013 AS BOTH REPAIRS REQUIRE THE APPLICATION OF POLYSULFIDE TO THE SAME CLOSEOUT AREAS. BASED ON THIS INFORMATION MTU INVESTIGATED ON THE WORK ORDERS ALREADY PERFORMED AND IDENTIFIED, THAT ON THE PARTS LISTED IN ATTACHMENT 1 MTU DID NOT APPLY POLYSULFIDE IN THE CLOSEOUT AREA BELOW THE ABRADABLE AS REQUESTED PER EM 72-00-24 REPAIR 003 AND 72-24-01 REPAIR 013.  FOLLOWING STEPS OF 72-00-24 REPAIR 003 AND 72-24-01 REPAIR 013 HAVE NOT BEEN PERFORMED: - REPLACEMENT OF THE FIBERGLASS AT THE CLOSE OUTS WITH POLYSULFIDE UNDER THE ABRADABLE INADVERTENTLY NOT PERFORMED, REFER TO SUBTASK 72-00-24-300-004 AND 72-24-01-350-129 - REPLACEMENT OF THE FIBERGLASS AT THE CLOSE OUTS WITH POLYSULFIDE IN THE VERTICAL PART UP TO THE FAN CASE INADVERTENTLY NOT PERFORMED, REFER TO SUBTASK 72-24-01-350-117 AND SUBTASK 72-00-24-300-004 FROM OUR INTERNAL RISK ASSESSMENT, MTU CONSIDERS THE MENTIONED MISSING STEPS AS NOT FLIGHT SAFETY RELEVANT, REQUIRING NO IMMEDIATE ACTIONS. THE RISK, THAT WAS IDENTIFIED, IS PRIMARILY, THAT THE MOISTURE CAN GET THROUGH THE GAP BETWEEN TWO ADJACENT TRENCH FILLERS, AND THE MOISTURE MIGHT LEAD TO CORROSION. THIS CORROSION CAN POTENTIALLY LEAD TO UN-SERVICEABILITY OF THE PART AT THE NEXT SHOP INSPECTION, BUT NO ULTIMATE FAILURE OF THE PART, WHICH WOULD LEAD TO A SAFETY RELEVANT EVENT. FURTHERMORE, FOR ALL IN SHOP HANDLED FAN STATOR MODULES, NO FINDINGS IN THE FIBERGLASS CLOSEOUTS WERE IDENTIFIED, WHICH WOULD MAKE A REPAIR MANDATORY. THE APPLICATION OF POLYSULFIDE AS PART OF REPAIR 003 AND 013 IS A PROACTIVE MEASURE TO PREVENT FUTURE ENTRY OF MOISTURE IN THE SPLIT LINE. MTU SHOP HANDLING GUIDE WORK SCOPE LEVEL TSO1 REQUIRED REPAIR 003 AS THIS PROACTIVE MEASURE. REPAIR 13 IS REQUIRED BASED ON FINDINGS PER EM INSPECTION.  MTU CONTACTED THE OEM FOR TECHNICAL SUPPORT AND TO CONFIRM THE RISK ASSESSMENT AS WELL AS TERMINATING ACTIONS SUGGESTED BY MTU, REFER TO CASE #02144932 OPENED 04. MARCH 2025.  EVALUATION AT GE IS STILL ONGOING, YET NO SAFETY CONCERN WAS RAISED BY THE OEM.  REVIEW OF MTU WORKING DOCUMENTATION TO ANALYZE MTU PROCESS. INFORMATION OF OEM AND CONSULTATION REGARDING CORRECT UNDERSTANDING OF DATA, REFER TO CASE  #02135752 AND #02135634.  CONSULTATION OF OEM TO VERIFY THE MTU SAFETY ASSESSMENT AND TO OBTAIN GUIDANCE FOR AFFECTED  HARDWARE, REFER TO CASE #02144932.  AN INTERNAL INVESTIGATION HAS BEEN INITIATED TO IDENTIFY THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE ERROR AND DEFINE APPROPRIATE CORRECTIVE AND PREVENTIVE ACTIONS. CUSTOMERS TO BE INFORMED ABOUT THE ISSUE BASED ON OEM FEEDBACK ON CASE #02144932.  DURING ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS THE ISHIKAWA- AND 5-WHY-METHOD WAS USED TO IDENTIFY THE ROOT  CAUSE OF THE INCORRECT POLYSULFIDE APPLICATION. WITHIN THE FRAMEWORK OF ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS THE FOLLOWING CONTRIBUTING FACTORS WERE IDENTIFIED: THE ERROR OCCURRED DURING THE WORK PLANNING PROCESS WHEN THE WORK PLANNER INTENDED TO TRANSFER THE REQUIREMENTS FROM THE ENGINE MANUAL REPAIR INTO MTU INTERNAL WORKING  DOCUMENTATION.  WHILE TRANSFERRING THE OEM REPAIR INFORMATION THE WORK PLANNER MISINTERPRETED THE ENGINE  MANUAL REQUIREMENTS REGARDING THE NECESSITY OF THE REPLACEMENT OF THE FIBERGLASS WITH POLYSULFIDE AT THE CLOSE OUTS UNDER THE ABRADABLE AND THE VERTICAL PART UP TO THE FAN CASE AS PART OF REPAIR 003 AND REPAIR 013 INCORRECTLY. THE FOLLOWING CONTRIBUTING FACTORS WERE IDENTIFIED: IN EM 72-00-24 REP. 003 THERE IS NO INDICATION OR INSTRUCTION TO REMOVE THE ABRADABLE. THE REQUIREMENTS FOR THE REMOVAL OF THE FIBERGLASS IS BASED ON THE PMI AND IS DESCRIBED IN EM 72-00-24 INSPECTION 002 AND WAS THEREFORE MISSED TO BE CONSIDERED WHEN REPAIR 003 WAS PLANNED. PMI AND MTU INTERNAL SHG REQUIRE TO PERFORM REPAIR 003, BUT AS THERE IS NO CLEAR REQUIREMENT IN REPAIR 003 THE INTENT TO REPLACE THE FIBERGLASS WITH POLYSULFIDE AT THE WHOLE LENGTH OF THE CLOSE OUTS AS PART OF THE REPAIR WAS NOT CORRECTLY IMPLEMENTED IN THE MTU INTERNAL WORKING  DOCUMENTATION.  THE EM 72-24-01 REPAIR 013 CONTAINS VARIOUS OPTIONAL REPAIRS AND ITS DESCRIPTION IS COMPLEX AND NOT EASILY UNDERSTANDABLE. ONE ELEMENT OF REPAIR 013 IS THE REPLACEMENT OF THE FIBERGLASS
WITH POLYSULFIDE AT THE CLOSE OUTS. DUE TO THE COMPLEX STRUCTURE AND THE INCORRECT INTERPRETATION OF REPAIR 013 THE REQUIREMENT TO REPLACE THE FIBERGLASS WITH POLYSULFIDE IN THE AFFECTED AREAS DESCRIBED ABOVE AS PART OF REPAIR 013 WAS MISSED BY THE WORK PLANNER.  THE ESM INSTRUCTIONS FOR REMOVING AND REAPPLYING THE ABRADABLE ARE IN RETROSPECT NOT  SUFFICIENTLY CLEAR AND STRUCTURED AND THEREFORE THE TRANSFER OF THE ESM INSTRUCTIONS TO MTU  INTERNAL WORK PLANS WAS INCORRECT.   IN THE LATER INDUSTRIALIZATION OF EM 72-24-01 REPAIR 013, THE INCLUDED NOTE REGARDING THE  DEFINITION OF THE PROCESSING AREA, BASED ON EXISTING EXPERIENCE AND THE COMPLEX NESTING OF MULTIPLE REPAIRS, WAS OVERLOOKED. BOTH PLANNED REPAIRS UNDERWENT A FOUR-EYE CHECK BY QUALIFIED STAFF (INCLUDING VERIFICATION AGAINST THE EM) AND A FIRST ARTICLE REVIEW BY THE RELEVANT PRODUCTION DEPARTMENT AND QUALITY CONTROL, WITHOUT THE ERROR BEING DETECTED. IT WAS VERIFIED, THAT ALL INVOLVED EMPLOYEES WERE FULLY TRAINED FOR THE TASKS TO BE PERFORMED AND EXPERIENCED IN THE ACTIVITY. ALL INTERNAL PROCESSES WERE CORRECTLY FOLLOWED AND DOCUMENTED. RELEVANT FA/FB DOCUMENTATION WAS REVIEWED AND FOUND CORRECT. THE WORK PLAN WAS REVISED TO CORRECTLY REFLECT THE POLYSULFIDE REPAIR. BASED ON THE WORK PLAN ALL FUTURE MODULES WILL BE INSPECTED AND REPAIRED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE EM REQUIREMENTS. THE CONTENT OF THE MTU SHOP HANDLING GUIDE WILL BE CHECKED AND IMPROVED WITH REGARDS TO THE DESCRIPTION OF THE REQUIREMENTS TO PERFORM POLYSULFIDE REPAIR 003 AND 013. ALL WORK PLANS AFFECTING GE90 FAN CASES WILL BE REVIEWED TO ENSURE, THAT THEY ARE IN LINE WITH EM AND MTU INTERNAL SHOP HANDLING GUIDE REQUIREMENTS.  THE ISSUE WILL BECOME A FOCUS IN SPOT CHECKS BY THE SUPERVISOR IN THE RESPECTIVE AREA. DURING THE INTERNAL AUDIT IN Q3 2025 IN THE FAN AREA THE IMPLEMENTATION OF ACTIONS AND
EFFECTIVENESS OF ACTIONS WILL BE REVIEWED TO ENSURE EFFECTIVENESS AND VERIFY COMPLIANCE.

WHILE TAXIING THE AIRCRAFT, THE PILOT EXPERIENCED A COMPLETE LOSS OF ENGINE CONTROL DUE TO A FAILURE OF THE THROTTLE AND MIXTURE ASSEMBLY. SPECIFICALLY, THE THROTTLE AND MIXTURE CONTROLS BECAME DISCONNECTED, RESULTING IN THE PILOT BEING UNABLE TO MANIPULATE ENGINE POWER SETTINGS.  UPON DISASSEMBLY OF THE CONTROL ASSEMBLY, IT WAS FOUND THAT THE PIVOT SHAFT—ON WHICH BOTH THE THROTTLE AND MIXTURE LEVERS ARTICULATE—HAD COMPLETELY BACKED OUT OF ITS HOUSING. THIS DISENGAGEMENT RENDERED THE THROTTLE AND MIXTURE LINKAGES INOPERATIVE.  FOLLOWING REASSEMBLY, IT WAS OBSERVED THAT ADJUSTING THE THROTTLE FRICTION KNOB CAUSED THE SINGLE RETAINING SCREW SECURING THE PIVOT ASSEMBLY TO BEGIN BACKING OUT. FURTHER INSPECTION OF ANOTHER TECNAM P2010 IN THE FLEET REVEALED THE SAME SCREW HAD ALSO BACKED OUT SIGNIFICANTLY, INDICATING A POTENTIAL SYSTEMIC ISSUE.  IT IS IMPORTANT TO NOTE THAT THERE IS CURRENTLY NO PROVISION TO SAFETY THIS CRITICAL FASTENER IN PLACE, RAISING CONCERNS ABOUT ITS LONG-TERM RELIABILITY AND THE POTENTIAL FOR RECURRENCE.

TOOK 15 MINUTES TO CLIMB TO 17,000 AND WERE LEVEL FOR APPROXIMATELY 25 MINUTES WHEN A RAPID SERIES OF BLAST NOISES CAME FROM THE ENGINE ACCOMPANIED BY LARGE AMOUNTS OF SPARKS CONTINUOUSLY EMANATING OUT OF THE EXHAUST. OUR POWER SETTING WERE LIKELY 1.5PSI TO 2PSI BELOW MAX TORQUE, AS THIS IS GENERALLY WHERE I LIKE TO SET THE POWER. OUR ITT’S WERE WELL WITHIN THE NORMAL RANGE (LIKELY AROUND 710) AND OUR NG’S WERE NORMAL ALSO. THESE SPECIFIC NUMBERS CAN BE PULLED. THERE WERE NO INDICATIONS THAT THE SURGES OR STALLS (WHICHEVER THEY WERE) AFFECTED THE ENGINE INDICATIONS, THOUGH I REDUCED POWER QUICKLY AFTER THE EVENT TO GET IT TO STOP. THE SEPARATOR WAS CLOSED IN VMC CONDITIONS. I REDUCED POWER IN HOPING TO FIND A SWEET SPOT WHERE THE BLASTS WERE NOT OCCURRING AND PULLED THE PCL BACK TO HAVE THE NG IN THE SINGLE DIGIT RANGE. THIS HAD THE EFFECT THAT I WAS LOOKING FOR WITH A CESSATION OF THE SURGES AND SPARKS FOR THE MOST PART. ANY POWER INPUTS THEREAFTER ON OUR WAY TO THE NEAREST AIRPORT BROUGHT BACK THE SURGES AND SPARKS. I FELT AS IF I COULD GET AN INCREASE IN POWER FROM THE ENGINE, AND DID SO A FEW TIMES, BUT THE SPARKING AND SURGE/STALLS INCREASED AS WELL.  THE SPARKS ALSO CONTINUED INTERMITTENTLY ON THE WAY TO THE AIRPORT, BUT NOT AS MANY AS WHEN EVENT INITIALLY STARTED. AROUND 5 MILES AWAY FROM THE AIRPORT WE DID START TO SMELL SMOKE, BUT NOT THAT WAS VISIBLE NOR SEEMED TO BE WORKING ITS WAY INTO THE COCKPIT TO ANY SIGNIFICANT DEGREE. THIS SMELL WAS BRIEF AND DISSIPATED QUICKLY. I INTENTIONALLY KEPT THE AIRCRAFT HIGH ON THE WAY TO OUR KAVP TO BETTER ENSURE MAKING THE AIRPORT IF THE ENGINE WERE TO QUIT. WE WERE SET UP FOR THE ILS AND VECTORED TO LOSE ALTITUDE. WE BROKE OUT OF AN OVERCAST LAYER WHICH MAY HAVE BEEN 2500 TO 3500’. I CALLED FOR THE GEAR AND FLAPS WHEN WE WERE MAYBE ¼ OF A MILE FROM THE RUNWAY TO ENSURE WE WOULD MAKE IT. I DID NOT USE BETA OR REVERSE AND WE ROLLED OUT NEAR THE FAR END OF THE RUNWAY.

NO SMOKE OR FIRE AND NO INDICATION INFLIGHT.  THE "CLIPS" THAT HOLD THIS ROD TO THE COWLING TOP HAVE LOOSENED THE GRIP ALLOWING THE ROD TO SLIP.  I HAVE SQUEEZED THESE CLIPS TO PREVENT THIS BUT OVER TIME THE CLIPS LOOSEN.  I HAVE TIGHTENED THEM AND APPLIED HEAT SHRINK TO THE ROD TO INCREASE THE GRIP IN THE CLIPS.  UPON THE NEXT ENGINE START THE ENTIRE SYSTEM WAS ELECTRICALLY DEAD AND WE DISCOVERED THE DIODES HAD SHORTED AND BURNED.  REPLACED THE DIODES BY USING NEW DIODES (4005 AS CALLED FOR IN THE PARTS MANUAL) INSPECTED WIRING AND SYSTEM WORKED WITH NO ANOMALIES.  I HAVE NOTICED THAT THIS COWLING HOLD OPEN LATCH/ROD IS LOOSE ON OTHER BONANZA'S.

CESSNA CITATION CE525 WITH GARMIN G3000 AVIONICS PACKAGE. AIRCRAFT DEPARTED SLC FOR FFZ. THE NAV DATA CYCLE RENEWED ON APRIL 17 BUT WAS AVAILABLE FOR DOWNLOAD 5 DAYS PRIOR. PILOT PERFORMED THE UPLOAD ON APRIL 15. A STEP IN THE UPLOAD PROCEDURE IS AVIONICS RESTART TO FORCE THE NEW DATA FROM THE CENTER MFD TO THE OUTSIDE PFD'S. THE STEP WAS PERFORMED, AND ALL INDICATIONS WERE THAT THE UPLOAD WAS COMPLETED AND SUCCESSFUL. ON THE NEXT FLIGHT THE PILOT WAS GIVEN THE ARCHZ 1 DEPARTURE WHICH USUALLY STARTS WITH A WESTBOUND TURN FROM RUNWAY 35 TO 260 DEGREES AND A CLIMB TO 9000 FT. THE WEATHER THAT DAY WAS SUCH THAT THE AIRCRAFT WAS IN THE CLOUDS WITHIN A FEW THOUSAND FEET AFTER TAKEOFF. THE TURN WAS COMPLETED AND THE AUTOPILOT ENGAGED. AT THAT POINT THE PILOT RECEIVED TWO CAS MESSAGES ON THE PFD, ONE READ "TERRAIN FAIL" AND THE OTHER READ "FMS FUEL MISMATCH". THEY BEGAN BLINKING. THE MESSAGES WERE AMBER INDICATING THAT ACTION NEEDED TO BE TAKEN BUT NOT IMMEDIATELY. THE PILOT WAS GIVEN A SW TURN TO SCANT AND A CLIMB TO FL230. HE ENTERED SCANT AND THE CLIMB INTO MY AUTOPILOT AND ENGAGED NAV.  THE AIRCRAFT BEGAN A TURN TO THE NW AND TO DESCEND. THE PILOT BEGAN TO FIGHT THE AUTOPILOT BUT IT WOULD NOT RESPOND CORRECTLY. THE PILOT EVENTUALLY DISCONNECTED THE AUTOPILOT AND BEGAN A TURN TO THE SW. THE AIRCRAFT WAS IN IMC WITH CAS SCREENS FLASHING, PICKING UP ICE AND THE PILOT WAS TRYING TO KEEP THE AIRCRAFT UNDER CONTROL WHILE ATTEMPTING TO GET THE AUTOPILOT TO COOPERATE.  EVENTUALLY THE PILOT REQUESTED A RETURN TO KSLC AND WAS GIVEN VECTORS TO THE ILS 34L. THE PILOT WAS ABLE LOAD THE APPROACH AND GET THE FMS TO GIVE FLIGHT DIRECTOR BARS TO FOLLOW THE APPROACH. THE CONTROLLER ASKED IF THE PILOT WANTED TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY WHICH HE DID. THE AIRCRAFT LANDED UNEVENTFULLY.  THE PILOT RE-ACCOMPLISHED THE UPLOAD WITH THE SD CARD IN THE AIRCRAFT AND REPOWERED THE AVIONICS, TWICE. AGAIN, THE SYSTEM INDICATED THAT THE UPLOAD WAS SUCCESSFUL. THE PILOT RESTARTED THE AIRCRAFT AND AGAIN ATTEMPTED THE FLIGHT. THE AVIONICS FUNCTIONED PROPERLY. THE AIRCRAFT AVIONICS WERE INSPECTED BY AN AVIONICS REPAIR STATION. ADDITIONAL FLIGHTS WERE ACCOMPLISHED WITH THE AVIONICS OPERATING PROPERLY.  THE PILOT RECOMMENDS RESTART SEVERAL TIMES AFTER AN UPLOAD AND MAKE SURETHE AVIONICS ARE SATISFIED AND STABLE.

REQUESTED FIRE DEPARTMENT FOAM RUNWAY & THEN MADE AN INTENTIONAL GEAR UP LANDING.  STATED THAT ON SHORT FINAL THEY PULLED MIXTURE, TURNED FUEL OFF, & LANDED. NOTED THE BELLCRANK ASSEMBLY (P/N 5041001) WAS SHEARED WITH EVIDENCE OF A CRACK/CORROSION PRESENT.  ACFT TOWED TO RAMP. REVIEW OF MX RECORDS SHOWED ACFT CURRENT WITH ALL REQUIRED INSPECTIONS & GEAR HAD BEEN CYCLED MULTIPLE TIMES ON JACKS WITH NO ISSUES NOTED PRIOR TO THE ACCIDENT.

AN AIR TRACTOR AT802A WAS INVOLVED IN A TAKE-OFF INCIDENT, CAUSING SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE. THE PIC LOOKED TO HIS LEFT AND RIGHT DURING TAKEOFF AND NOTICED THE FLAPS WERE RETRACTING UNCOMMANDED AFTER SELECTING 20 DEGREES FOR TAKEOFF. ASI DISCOVERED THAT THE FLAP ACTUATOR ASSEMBLY COUPLING, PART NUMBER B100-06, WHICH SERVES AS THE CONNECTION BETWEEN THE ELECTRIC FLAP MOTOR AND THE ACTUATOR LYING AT THE BOTTOM OF THE AIRCRAFT, WAS BROKEN. UPON EXAMINATION, IT WAS FOUND THAT THE METAL KEYS WITHIN THE COUPLING HAD SHEARED OFF, LEADING TO THE FAILURE OF THIS CRITICAL COMPONENT. ACCORDING TO AIR TRACTOR SERVICE LETTER (SL) 260, WHICH PROVIDES DETAILED INFORMATION REGARDING THE FLAP ACTUATOR COUPLING, THE MANUFACTURER RECOMMENDS REPLACING THE COUPLING AFTER 400 HOURS OF OPERATION. HOWEVER, IN THIS INSTANCE, THE COUPLING FAILED AT 575.7 HOURS, SIGNIFICANTLY EXCEEDING THE RECOMMENDED REPLACEMENT INTERVAL.

THEY WOULD BALANCE FOR A SECOND, SO WE'D TURN THE FUEL SWITCH OFF BUT THEN THE NEXT SECOND, THEY WOULD SHOW 400LBS DIFFERENCE OR MORE. RAN EMERGENCY CHECKLIST AND PUT R ENG THROTTLE TO CUTOFF. SETUP SINGLE ENGINE APPROACH AND LANDED SAFELY. UPON LANDING AND BEFORE SHUTDOWN NOTED R FUEL QUANTITY SHOWED 690LBS WHILE L SHOWED 560LBS. THE RH ENGINE WAS STARTED SEVERAL MORE TIMES AND THE ISSUE WAS NOT DUPLICATED.

TESTED THE PLUG AND IT DID NOT FIRE. BORESCOPE OF THE CYLINDER LOOKED OK. A NEW PLUG WAS PUT IN. JUNE  22ND 3HRS INTO A FLIGHT THE PILOT REPORTED THE ENGINE STARTED RUNNING ROUGH. BACKING OFF ENGINE POWER AND RUNNING RICHER THE ENGINE SMOOTHED OUT. ENGINE MONITOR DATA FROM THE PAST 4 FLIGHTS SHOWED INTERMITTENT ELEVATED #4 EGT. THE #4 SPARK PLUGS WERE REMOVED AND FOUND THAT BOTH CENTER ELECTRODES WERE MISSING. BOTH PLUGS WERE TESTED ON A BENCH WITH NO SPARK. THE PLUGS ARE TEMPEST P/N URHB32S - THEY WERE INSTALLED IN OCTOBER 2020 AND HAVE  ABOUT 709 HOURS ON THEM. THE FIRST PLUG FAILED IN OCTOBER 2024, THE SECOND PAIR OF PLUGS FAILED 68 HOURS LATER ON JUNE 22ND 2025. AFTER THE FIRST FAILURE I CONTACTED THE MANUFACTURER WHO SAID THEY HAD NOT SEEN A FAILURE LIKE THAT AND ASKED ME TO SEND THE SPARK TO THEM FOR INSPECTION. THEY SENT A REPLACEMENT BACK. I DID NOT HEAR BACK FROM THEM ON WHAT HAPPENED. I HAVE CONTACTED THE MANUFACTURER AGAIN ABOUT THE TWO FAILURES. THEY HAVE OFFERED TO REPLACE ALL 12 PLUGS. I HAVE NOT HEARD BACK FROM THEM ON WHAT COULD HAVE CAUSED 3 PLUGS TO FAIL LIKE THIS. I SPOKE WITH THE  MANUFACTURER (POWERMASTER ENGINES), THEY STATED THEY SAW A RASH OF FAILURES LIKE THIS WITH THIS PARTICULAR PLUG A FEW YEARS BACK. MY CONCERN HERE IS THAT THERE IS A BAD BATCH OF PLUGS FLOATING AROUND. WE HAVE LOST 3 PLUGS IN 68 HOURS - TWO OF THEM AT THE SAME TIME IN THE SAME CYLINDER. WE WERE FORTUNATE TO GET THE PLANE BACK DOWN SAFELY WITH NO APPARENT DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE - THIS COULD HAVE BEEN WORSE.

DEFECT WILL NOT EASILY VISIBLE TO TECHNICIANS BECAUSE OF THE DUCT POSITION AND DAMPING MATERIAL AND NO IDEA HOW MANY OTHER CL-605 SERIES AIRCRAFT FLYING WITH CRACKED AIRINLET ASSEMBLY.  ISSUE HAS BEEN REPORTED TO BOMBARDIER.

DURING TAKEOFF FROM BLUE GRASS AIRPORT (KLEX), THE PILOT REPORTED THAT UPON RETRACTING THE LANDING GEAR, THE LANDING GEAR LEVER RED UNSAFE LIGHT ILLUMINATED, ACCOMPANIED BY AN AURAL GEAR WARNING. THE PILOT EXTENDED THE LANDING GEAR, WHICH RESULTED IN THREE DOWN-AND-LOCKED INDICATIONS. HOWEVER, WHEN ATTEMPTING TO LOWER THE FLAPS, THE PILOT NOTED THAT THE FLAP MOTOR CIRCUIT BREAKER HAD POPPED.   THE AIRCRAFT WAS PLACED ON JACKS FOR A GEAR RETRACTION TEST, DURING WHICH MAINTENANCE VERIFIED THE SAME GEAR UNSAFE WARNING LIGHT AND AURAL WARNING. THE FLAP MOTOR CIRCUIT BREAKER WAS OBSERVED TO POP APPROXIMATELY 20 SECONDS AFTER BEING RESET ON THE GROUND. TROUBLESHOOTING REVEALED THAT UNPLUGGING THE CANNON PLUG FROM THE FLAP SWITCH BOX IN THE RIGHT WING FLAP-WELL ELIMINATED THE WARNING AND PREVENTED THE CIRCUIT BREAKER FROM POPPING. IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE FLAP WARNING POSITION SWITCH, WHICH ACTIVATES THE GEAR WARNING WHEN FLAPS ARE EXTENDED, WAS STUCK IN THE DOWN POSITION, CAUSING A FALSE GEAR UNSAFE INDICATION AND TRIPPING THE FLAP CIRCUIT BREAKER.   NEW FLAP WARNING POSITION SWITCH (P/N: BZ7RW82255518T) AND FLAP MOTOR (P/N: 101-384040, S/N: 4221) WERE INSTALLED AND RIGGED. SUBSEQUENT TESTING CONFIRMED PROPER GEAR RETRACTION WITHOUT WARNINGS, AND THE FLAP MOTOR CIRCUIT BREAKER NO LONGER TRIPPED.  THE AIRCRAFT WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE FOLLOWING SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF ALL TESTS AND VERIFICATION OF PROPER OPERATION.

ON 09/2/25 WE WERE DEPARTING RUNWAY 21 AT KCNM. AT V1 DURING OUR TAKE ROLL WE HEARD A VERY AUDIBLE IMPACT OR “ THUD” AIRCRAFT RIGHT. THE IMPACT INDUCED A SIGNIFICANT RIGHT YAW. THERE WAS ALSO A MOMENTARY EICAS CAUTION MESSAGE. IT CLEARED BEFORE BEING ABLE TO IDENTIFY IT. WE BELIEVE IT WAS “ENGINE TLA NOT IN TAKE OFF”. THIS WAS PROBABLY INDUCED BY MY HANDS BEING PULLED BACK SLIGHTLY DURING THE INITIAL IMPACT OR YAW.  CONTINUED THE TAKE OFF AND PROCEEDED THE INITIAL CLIMB SEQUENCE WITH OUT INCIDENT. OUR INITIAL DIAGNOSIS WAS A POSSIBLE BLOWN TIRE. ALL ENGINE INSTRUMENTS WERE NORMAL. WE PROCEEDED TO KMAF FOR SEVERAL FACTORS AFFECTING SAFETY. ONCE IN “CRUISE” WE CONTACTED AIRCRAFT AT CNM AND THE AIRPORT STAFF TO LOOK FOR DEBRIS ON RUNWAY 21. ALL REPORTS WERE NEGATIVE ON DEBRIS. WE BRIEFED THE FLIGHT ATTENDANTS AND PASSENGERS FOR A POSSIBLE “ABNORMAL” LANDING. WE COMMUNICATED WITH MAF APPROACH ABOUT OUR CONDITION AND THEY ADVISED THEY WOULD HAVE RESCUE SERVICES ON STAND BY. WE COORDINATED WITH MAF ATC AND CONDUCTED A LOW APPROACH USING 34L RNAV WITH THE GEAR DOWN. THE APPROACH WAS CONDUCTED AND MIDLAND REPORTED THEY DID NOT OBSERVE ANY ABNORMALITIES. WE THEN CONDUCTED A NORMAL LANDING WITHOUT INCIDENT. UPON PARKING AND ENGINE SHUT DOWN WE CONDUCTED AN INSPECTION. WE OBSERVED INDICATIONS OF A BIRD STRIKE ON THE NUMBER 2 ENGINE. THIS WAS FURTHER VALIDATED BY AN EICAS CAUTION MESSAGE “ENG 2 T2 HEAT FAIL”. THESE OBSERVATIONS LED US TO BELIEVE THERE WAS SUFFICIENT INDICATIONS OF A BIRD BEING INGESTED IN THE RIGHT ENGINE. THESE FACTORS WERE DELIVERED TO THE DIRECTOR OF AVIATION AND DIRECTOR OF MAINTENANCE WHO COLLECTIVELY AGREED TO GROUND THE AIRCRAFT PENDING INSPECTION. ENGINE WAS BOROSCOPED WITH NO DISCREPANCIES NOTED.

ON JUNE 12TH, 2025, PHOENIX AIR GROUP, INC. (PAG) WAS TRANSPORTING PASSENGERS FROM POINT MUGU NAVAL AIR STATION (KNTD) TO SAN NICOLAS ISLAND NAVAL OUTLYING FIELD (KNSI) USING  AIRCRAFT N405PA.  ONCE THE AIRCRAFT BEGAN CLIMBING TO ITS CRUISE ALTITUDE, CAPTAIN 1 (CA1) AND FIRST OFFICER 1 (FO1) NOTICED SIGNS OF A LEFT ENGINE FAILURE AND RESPONDED TO AN ENGINE FAILURE. FLIGHT ATTENDANT 1 (FA1) NOTIFIED CA1 OF THE ENGINE FIRE, AND CA1 ATTEMPTED TO PUT OUT THE ENGINE FIRE WHILE FO1 DECLARED AN EMERGENCY TO AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL (ATC). CA1 SUCCESSFULLY EXTINGUISHED THE FIRE MID-FLIGHT. FIRE TRUCKS WERE ON STANDBY AS THE AIRCRAFT WAS LANDING, THE AIRCRAFT LANDED SAFELY, AND THE FIRE DEPARTMENT CONFIRMED THAT THE FIRE HAD BEEN EXTINGUISHED AND THAT THE AIRCRAFT WAS SAFE TO RETURN TO THE TERMINAL TO UNLOAD PASSENGERS. ENGINE 1 SUSTAINED SUBSTANTIAL FIRE DAMAGE, BUT THE FIRE WAS CONTAINED WITHOUT AIRFRAME FIRE OR EXPLOSION. BASED ON EXAMINATION BY PHOENIX AIR GROUP’S MAINTENANCE TECHNICIANS, EVIDENCE INDICATES THAT THE EVENT WAS PRECIPITATED BY A SUDDEN STOPPAGE OF THE CORE COMPONENTS OF THE ENGINE’S ROTATING ASSEMBLY, CONSISTENT WITH A MAIN SHAFT BEARING FAILURE. THIS SUDDEN STOPPAGE DISRUPTED THE ANNULAR COMBUSTION PATTERN WITHIN THE BURNER CAN, PERMITTING UNBURNED FUEL TO MIGRATE INTO THE TAILPIPE, WHERE IT IGNITED. ONCE THE CREW EXECUTED THE ENGINE SHUTDOWN AND FIRE CHECKLIST THE TAILPIPE FIRE EXTINGUISHED.

FLT NUMBER: DVR023, ENGINE FAILURE AND EMERGENCY LANDING.  SHORTLY AFTER DEPARTURE FROM BON, THE CREW EXPERIENCED A LOSS OF FUEL PRESSURE AND OBSERVED A DECREASING OIL PRESSURE ON THE LEFT-HAND (LH) ENGINE. DUE TO THESE CRITICAL INDICATIONS, A PRECAUTIONARY SHUTDOWN WAS PERFORMED AND A MAYDAY CALL WAS ISSUED. THE AIRCRAFT RETURNED TO BON FOR AN EMERGENCY LANDING AND THE AFFECTED LH ENGINE WAS FEATHERED PRIOR TO LANDING.  THE LH ENGINE WAS DECLARED UNSERVICEABLE (U/S) AND SUBSEQUENTLY REPLACED.  A DUPLICATE INSPECTION, INCLUDING A RETURN TO SERVICE INSPECTION (RII), WAS PERFORMED ON THE REPLACEMENT ENGINE.  A MALFUNCTION DEFECT REPORT (MDR) WAS SUBMITTED ACCORDING TO CCAR 5.4.1.5,  3 DAYS AFTER THE INCIDENT. DURING A PLANNED FLIGHT FROM FORT WORTH MEACHAM (KFTW) TO KENOSHA, WI (KENW), THE PILOT OF A PIPER PA-46-310P MALIBU EXPERIENCED A FUEL SYSTEM ANOMALY. APPROXIMATELY 3 HOURS INTO THE FLIGHT AT FL230, THE PILOT OBSERVED THE INDICATED FUEL QUANTITY DECREASING THREE TIMES FASTER THAN THE FUEL TOTALIZER SHOWED. SUSPECTING A LEAK, THE PILOT DIVERTED TO AURORA, IL (KARR) TO REMAIN CLEAR OF CHICAGO CLASS B AIRSPACE.   DURING DESCENT, FUEL GAUGES SHOWED CRITICALLY LOW QUANTITIES. AN EMERGENCY WAS DECLARED WITH CHICAGO APPROACH. ON FINAL, THE ENGINE BEGAN SURGING AND QUIT COMPLETELY WITH LESS THAN 5 GALLONS INDICATED. THE PILOT EXECUTED A SUCCESSFUL DEAD-STICK LANDING ON RUNWAY 27 AT KARR WITH NO DAMAGE. POST-LANDING INSPECTION REVEALED BLUE FUEL STAINING IN THE NOSE GEAR WELL.  MAINTENANCE INVESTIGATION BY J.A. AIR CENTER CONFIRMED THE ENGINE-DRIVEN FUEL PUMP HAD FAILED, LEAKING FUEL INTO THE WHEEL WELL NEAR THE EXHAUST CROSSOVER TUBE, PRESENTING A FIRE HAZARD. THE PUMP WAS REPLACED AND THE AIRCRAFT RETURNED TO SERVICE.

DURING FLIGHT, PILOT REPORTED FUEL FLOW DISCREPANCY AND ENGINE ROUGHNESS AND RETUNRED TO BASE FOR A PRECAUTIONARY, ALBEIT IF VERY STRESSFUL, LANDING.  UPON INSPECTION OF THE FUEL FLOW SENSOR ( PART OF THE JPI 930 ENGINE INSTRUMENTAION - STC SA01435SA ) IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE FLOW METER PINS ( A FLOSCAN 201 UNIT PROVIDED FROM JPI ) HAD BEEN INCORRECTLY TERMINATED. THE MALE PINS HAD BEEN CRIMPED ON WIRES THAT WERE STRIPPED TO LONG. THESE UNITS WERE SHIPPED FROM JPI PINNED AND INSIDE A TERMINAL BLOCK, MAKING VISUAL INSPECTION DIFFICULT WITHOUT PIN REMOVAL. ADDITIONALY, WHO UNPINS ITEMS SHIPPED FROM THE "MANUFACTURER" JUST TO CHECK-   WHILE THE PART OF THE PIN THAT WAS SUPPOSED TO BE ON THE BARE WIRE CONDUCTOR WAS CRIMPED CORRECTLY, THE SECOND CRIMP WHICH IS SUPPOSED TO BE ON THE INSULATION ( STRAIN RELIEF ) WAS ALSO CRIMPED ON THE CONDUCTOR, WHICH IS INCORRECT.  THE SECOND CRIMP WAS ALSO LOOSE, AS THE THE INSULATION WHICH WOULD NOMALLY BE A PART OF THE OVERALL THICKNESS, WAS ABSCENT. THIS LOOSE CRIMP, AND ABSCENT STRAIN RELIEF , ALLOWED THE WIRES TO FLEX AND EVENTAULLY BREAK. WHILE ONLY ONE OF THE THREE WIRES BROKE, THE OTHERS HAD LESS THAN 25% OF THIER STRANDS INTACT.  SUBSEQUENT INSECTIONS OF OTHER AC IN OUR FLEET, WITH SIMILAR FLOSCAN UNITS FROM THE SAME STC, REVEALED 2 OTHER UNITS WITH THE SAME ISSUE.  IN TOTAL, WE FOUND 3 FLOSCAN 201 UNITS ( SN'S 218375, 223453, AND 230659 ) ALL WITH THE SAME MISCRIMPED PINS.  WE HAD AT LEAST ONE ADDITIONAL UNIT THAT WAS REMOVED PREVIOUSLY "INOP" THAT WE COULDNT VERIFY AS IT WAS DISCARDED.

SEAT BACK CAM RETAINING PINS LOOSE, MISSING AND OR SHEARED FOUND SAFETY-WIRED IN PLACE. THERE APPEARS TO BE MANY OF THESE INFINITE ADJUSTABLE LOWER SEAT FRAMES WITH THE NAS SPLIT-PINS SAFETY-WIRED IN PLACE. THERE IS NO REQUIREMENT TO ADD SAFETY-WIRE TO THESE SPLIT PINS AND IS A POOR MAINTENANCE PRACTICE AS IT MASK THE ISSUE OF LOOSE PINS BEING HELD IN PLACE. THEREFORE, DURING PERIODIC INSPECTIONS A LOOSE & MIGRATING PIN IS RETAINED UNTIL FAILURE OF THE SEAT BACK WHEN IT EVENTUALLY FAILS ALLOWING THE SEAT BACK TO RELEASE COMPLETELY. THE CONCERN IS, IF THIS HAPPENS DURING TAKE-OFF ROLL THERE COULD BE COMPLETE LOSS OF CONTROL OF THE AIRCRAFT. I HAVE BEEN FINDING BETWEEN 50% & UP TO 80% OF THE RETENTION MEANS FAILED UPON INITIAL INSPECTION. ALSO DISCOVERED CRACKS IN THE SEAT BACK CAM ITSELF FROM SHEARED PINS FRACTURING THE RETENTION PIN HOLE OPENING. LOOSE SEAT PINS WILL MIGRATE AND UPON VISUAL SCHEDULED INSPECTION PERIOD CAN BE DISCOVERED & REPLACED ON AN AS-NEEDED BASIS. ANY ADJUSTABLE SEATS FOUND WITH SAFETY-WIRE RETAINING THE SPLIT-PINS SHOULD BE IMMEDIATELY REMOVED AND INSPECTED FOR SECURITY.  NOTE, THIS AFFECTS ALL CESSNA MODEL ACFT WITH ADJUSTABLE SEATING PILOT, CO-PILOT AND PASSENGER SEATING. THE PIN INSP SHOULD BE INCORPORATED INTO AD 2011-10-09 TO REMOVE SAFETY-WIRE IF FOUND AND VERIFY SECURITY OF RETAINING PINS. THERE ARE MULTIPLE SIZE P4-P6 PINS THROUGHOUT THE SEAT BOTTOM ASSEMBLY WITH VARIED LENGTH. PICTURES OF VARIOUS FAILURES AVAILABLE UPON REQUEST. * IN ADDITION I HAVE FOUND NON-NAS REPLACEMENTS (HARDWARE STORE) SPLIT PINS INSTALLED IN LIEU OF MIL-SPEC HARDWARE. THIS TYPE OF UNAPPROVED HARDWARE IS MADE OF SUB-STANDARD TIN WITH THIN WALL MATERIAL. SINCE FURNISHINGS ARE CONSIDERED OWNER PREVENTATIVE MAINTENANCE AND MANY INTERIOR SHOPS DONT UTILIZE CERTIFIED A&P LICENSE PERSONNEL THERE SEEMS TO BE A COMMON PRACTICE OF UTILIZING IMPROPER HARDWARE. TRANSPORTING PASSENGERS FROM KNTD TO KNSI. ONCE THE ACFT BEGAN CLIMBING TO CRUISE ALTITUDE, CAPT & 1ST OFFICER  NOTICED SIGNS OF A LT ENGINE FAILURE & RESPONDED TO AN ENGINE FAILURE. FA1 NOTIFIED CAPT OF THE ENG FIRE, & CAPT ATTEMPTED TO PUT OUT THE FIRE WHILE 1ST OFF DECLARED AN EMERGENCY TO ATC. CAPT SUCCESSFULLY EXTINGUISHED FIRE MID-FLIGHT.  ACFT LANDED SAFELY,  FIRE DEPART CONFIRMED FIRE EXTINGUISHED. ENGINE 1 SUSTAINED SUBSTANTIAL FIRE DAMAGE, BUT FIRE WAS CONTAINED WITHOUT AIRFRAME FIRE OR EXPLOSION. BASED ON EXAMINATION BY PAGS MAINTENANCE TECHS, EVIDENCE INDICATES THAT EVENT WAS PRECIPITATED BY A SUDDEN STOPPAGE OF CORE COMPONENTS OF ENGINE’S ROTATING ASSY, CONSISTENT WITH A MAIN SHAFT BEARING FAILURE. THIS SUDDEN STOPPAGE DISRUPTED THE ANNULAR COMBUSTION PATTERN WITHIN THE BURNER CAN, PERMITTING UNBURNED FUEL TO MIGRATE INTO THE TAILPIPE, WHERE IT IGNITED. ONCE THE CREW EXECUTED SHUTDOWN & FIRE CHECKLIST THE TAILPIPE FIRE EXTINGUISHED.

WHILE MAKING AN INITIAL LANDING AT KAUS, THE TOUCHDOWN OF NLG DIDN'T FEEL THE SAME AS OTHER IN THIS ACFT. ASKED AUSTIN TOWER TO ASK OPS CAR DRIVING BY,  TO TAKE A LOOK WITH THEIR SPOTLIGHT AT THE GEAR), THEY DID AND DIDN'T SEE ANYTHING ON THE GEAR OR  LEAKING FROM THE GEAR. I TAXIED TO MILLION AIR WITH NO STEERING ISSUES. I GOT OUT OF THE PLANE TO DO  USUAL WALK AROUND WITH BIG FLASHLIGHT AND PAID EXTRA ATTENTION TO THE FRONT WHEEL WELL. I DIDN'T FIND  TRASH, ANY LEAKS, OR ANYTHING THAT APPEARED TO BE BROKEN. I CALLED AFTER I GOT INSIDE TO TELL HIM  OF THE WEIRD EXPERIENCE, AND SAID WHO KNOWS WHAT IT COULD HAVE BEEN. SINCE I WENT OVER THE  EXTENSIVE LIST OF THINGS THAT I LOOKED AT AND CHECKED, HE THOUGHT TOO THAT ALL WAS PROBABLY GOOD.  WE THEN DEPARTED KAUS FOR KELP ONCE THE MED CREW RETURNED, TAXIED AND TURNED ON TAXIWAYS  AND RUNWAY JUST FINE SO I THOUGHT NOTHING ELSE OF IT. DEPARTED AUSTIN AREA WITHOUT EVENT. KELP THEN  CLEARED ME TO LAND ON 26L. THE MAINS TOUCHED DOWN AS USUAL BUT WHEN IT CAME TIME FOR THE NOSE  WHEEL TO TOUCH, HAD NO STEERING WITH RUDDER PEDALS.   HEARD WAS A SKIDDING TIRE & PLANE PULLING HARD TO RT  (NOSE WHEEL WAS TURNED TO  RIGHT). USING BETA ON LT ENGINE & POWER TO RT ENGINE TO KEEP 4LK ON RUNWAY & STANDING HARD ON BRAKES TO PREVENT 4LK FROM DRIFTING OFF OF RUNWAY. TRIED TO USE RUDDER PEDALS & DIFF BRAKING TO MOVE PLANE IN A DIFFERENT DIRECTION, & ALL THE  AIRCRAFT COULD DO IS STRUGGLE TO PLOUGH IN A SLOW FORWARD MOVEMENT.  CALLED TOWER TO DISPATCH A CLOSE BY OPS TRUCK TO SEE WHAT IT LOOKED LIKE AS FAR AS THE INFLATION OF THE TIRES SO I COULD MOVE PLANE OFF OF RUNWAY WITHOUT FURTHER DAMAGE.  OPS VEHICLE CONFIRMED  THE NOSE WHEEL WAS AT A 90 DEGREES TO PLANE, SHUTDOWN ENGINES.

THE AIRCRAFT WENT INTO MAINTENANCE WITH ANOTHER VENDOR WHO PERFORMED A MLG CAMBER CHECK AND FOUND THE CAMBER OUT OF ADJUSTMENT. UPON FURTHER INSPECTION, TECHS FOUND THAT THE KEYLOCK WAS NOT ENGAGED IN THE ACTUATOR SHAFT. DURING SUBSEQUENT INVESTIGATION BY DUNCAN, IT IS DETERMINED THAT THIS IS NOT AN ISOLATED INCIDENT TO JUST THIS AIRCRAFT.  RESEARCH HAS INDICATED THAT AT LEAST 4 DIFFERENT LOOSE ROD END JAM NUTS HAVE BEEN FOUND LOOSE DURING INSPECTIONS PERFORMED BY DUNCAN DATING BACK TO 2024.  MOST RECENTLY A 5TH AIRCRAFT, N565QS, ARRIVED OCT 12 WITH A LOOSE JAM NUT.  EXANIMATING THE LOCK KEYS FOUND WITH LOOSE JAM NUTS SHOW ONLY ABOUT 1/32 OF AN INCH ENGAGEMENT WITH THE ACTUATOR PISTON NOTCH (INDICATED BY WEAR AREA OF LOCK KEY).  IT'S ALSO BELIEVED THAT MULTIPLE R&R OF THE ROD END FOR THE TASK CARD INSPECTION, ACTUATOR VIBRATION FROM NORMAL USE, AND NOT CHANGING THE LOCK KEY AT EVERY INSPECTION ALSO CONTRIBUTES TO THE LOCK KEY FAILING AND ALLOWING THE ACTUATOR PISTON TO ROTATE AND LOOSING UP FROM THE JAM NUT.  THE 32-10-00-2201 RH MAIN LANDING GEAR ACTUATOR ROD END DETAILED INSPECTION IS A DISCRETIONARY MAINTENANCE 48-MONTH ITEM PUBLISHED BY TEXTRON FOR OPERATION IN HIGH CORROSION ENVIRONMENT.  WE TYPICALLY DON'T SEE LOOSE JAM NUTS ON OTHER AIRCRAFT THAT DON'T HAVE THIS INSPECTION PERFORMED. IT'S NOT BELIEVED THAT IS CAUSED BY IMPROPER MAINTENANCE, BUT A COMBINATION OF INSUFFICIENT KEY ENGAGEMENT, NORMAL OPERATIONAL WEAR, AND NOT REPLACING THE KEY LOCK AT EVERY INSPECTION.

POST-FLIGHT INSPECTION FOUND A SIGNIFICANT HYDRAULIC FLUID LEAK FROM THE LH ENGINE HYDRAULIC FILTER ASSEMBLY (PUROLATOR, P/N 460-635). INVESTIGATION REVEALED THE O-RING (MS28778-16) HAD FAILED BY EXTRUDING FROM THE HOUSING. THE O-RING WAS FOUND PINCHED BETWEEN THE FILTER BOWL AND HOUSING MATING SURFACES, NOT SEATED IN ITS INTENDED GROOVE. THIS IS A RECURRING FLEET-WIDE SAFETY ISSUE. OUR FLEET PREVIOUSLY REMOVED THE FACET-MANUFACTURED FILTERS DUE TO KNOWN CATASTROPHIC THREAD CRACKING (REF: CASA AWB 29-003). THE "OLDER" PUROLATOR-STYLE FILTERS, NOW IN USE, ARE FAILING DUE TO THIS O-RING RETENTION/INSTALLATION ISSUE. BOTH AVAILABLE DESIGNS FOR THIS COMPONENT HAVE KNOWN FAILURE MODES THAT LEAD TO THE SAME UNSAFE CONDITION: TOTAL LOSS OF MAIN HYDRAULIC PRESSURE. THIS IS THE 4TH SIMILAR HYDRAULIC/FILTER EVENT IN ABOUT 6 MONTHS IN OUR PA-31 FLEET, BUT THE FIRST BEING ENTERED IN THE FAA SDR SYSTEM. BECAUSE OF THE RECURRENCE, SHORT TIME-IN-SERVICE, AND DIRECT EFFECT ON GEAR EXTENSION, WE BELIEVE THIS REPRESENTS A FLEET-RELEVANT FAILURE MODE AND ARE REPORTING IT SO FAA CAN AGGREGATE SIMILAR CASES AND CONSIDER GUIDANCE.

THE CREW THEN RAN THROUGH THE QRH AND WAS ABLE TO STABILIZE CABIN PRESSURE WITH MANUAL MODE. THE AIRCRAFT SAFELY RETURNED TO KDAL. THE CABIN PRESSURE AUTO MODE WAS MELED AND THE AIRCRAFT WAS FLOWN TO KELP FOR MAINTENANCE. UPON ARRIVING IN ELP, THE PRESSURIZATION WAS TESTED AND THE ISSUE WAS DUPLICATED. WE TURNED THE BATTERY MASTER ON TO TEST A LANDING LIGHT THAT WAS REPORTED TO BE OUT. AFTER ABOUT ONE MINUTE OF THE BATTERY MASTER BEING ON, LARGE AMOUNTS OF SMOKE CAME FROM THE LEFT ENGINE. TROUBLESHOOTING FOUND THAT THE ALTERNATOR OUTPUT WIRE WAS SHIELDED AND VERY OLD. IT HAD DETERIORATED TO THE POINT WHERE THE POWER FROM THE BATTERY SHORTED TO THE SHIELD OF THE WIRE ROUGHLY ONE MINUTE AFTER POWER WAS APPLIED TO THE AIRCRAFT. THE SHORT CAUSED THE WIRE TO ALMOST COMPLETELY BURN THROUGH.

CREW DONNED MASKS AND STARTED AN EMERGENCY DESCENT. DURING THIS PROCESS THE COPILOT PULLED THE THROTTLES TO IDLE AND PULLED SPEED BRAKES ONCE WE STARTED THE EMERGENCY DESCENT WE STARTED THE PROCESS OF CONTACTING ATC FOR INSTRUCTIONS. CREW CONFIRMED WITH ATC THAT KGSO WAS OUR BEST OPTION. CREW DESCENDED INTO GSO WITHOUT FURTHER ISSUES.

DURING ROUTINE FLIGHT OPERATION THERE WAS A SUDDEN DECREASE IN ENGINE POWER AND A RISE IN VIBRATION WAS FELT, SO THE AIRCRAFT MADE A PRECAUTIONARY UNSCHEDULED LANDING AND SHUT DOWN WITHOUT INCIDENT. UPON INSPECTION OF THE AIRCRAFT IT WAS FOUND THAT ONE OF TWO ENGINE GOVERNOR, FUEL CONTROL PNEUMATIC CIRCUIT DAMPING CAPACITORS HAD BROKEN OFF, THEREBY OPENING THE AIR CIRCUIT AND SUBSEQUENTLY CAUSING A LOSS OF COMMUNICATION BETWEEN THE POWER TURBINE GOVERNOR AND THE FUEL CONTROL UNIT. THIS LOSS OF AIR SIGNAL TO THE FUEL CONTROL CAUSED IT TO SEE LESS OF A POWER DEMAND FROM THE GOVERNOR AND POWER WAS REDUCED ACCORDINGLY.  BELIEVE THE VIBRATION THAT WAS FELT BY THE CREW WAS CAUSED BY A REDUCTION IN ROTOR RPM AS THE POWER DROOPED. THE PRIMARY PURPOSE OF THESE CAPACITORS IS TO DAMPEN ANY SURGES IN SENSE AIR PRESSURE TO MINIMIZE GOVERNOR FLUCTUATIONS. THEY ARE BASICALLY AIR ACCUMULATORS. THE CAPACITORS ARE PART OF AN STC INSTALLATION (STC# SR00805SE) WHICH CHANGED THE POWERPLANT FROM A SAFRAN ARRIEL 1B TO A HONEYWELL LTS101-600A-3A. THE STC MAINTENANCE & OVERHAUL MANUAL SUPPLEMENT RECOMMENDS A 5000 HOUR SERVICE LIFE FOR THE CAPACITORS (P/N 366A54-1088-00), AND (P/N 350A54-1091-00). THE SPECIFIC CAPACITOR THAT FAILED WAS (P/N 366A54-1088-00). THE FAILED CAPACITOR HAD 4367.8 HOURS TOTAL TIME IN SERVICE, WITH 632.2 HOURS OF SERVICE LIFE REMAINING. THE STC HOLDER NOW PRODUCES REPLACEMENT CAPACITORS OF AN IMPROVED DESIGN THAT REINFORCES THE AREA PRONE TO BREAKAGE.

ATTEMPTED RESTART ENGINE 1,  UNSUCCESSFUL, ABORTED START.  ENGINE RE-LIT ON IT'S OWN  AND APPEARED TO BE FUNCTIONING NORMALLY;  DID NOT INCREASE POWER  IN A CONTINUOUS DESCENT. DUE TO THE STRONG GUSTING WINDS, DETERMINED A DUAL ENGINE APPROACH WOULD BE SAFEST IN THESE CONDITIONS, WITH THE PM CLOSELY MONITORING ENGINE FUNCTION TO TOUCHDOWN.  LANDING WAS UNEVENTFUL AND WE TAXIED TO THE FBO WITHOUT FURTHER INCIDENT.

AFTER LEVELING OFF FROM TAKEOFF WE STARTED NOTICING THE SMELL OF FUEL WHICH SEEMED TO BE COMING FROM THE CABIN AREA OF THE AIRCRAFT. INITIALLY WE TURNED OFF THE HEAT AND SELECTED OUTSIDE AIR FOR THE CABIN AND COCKPIT. WE TRIED DIFFERENT COMBINATIONS OF BLEED AIR AND OUTSIDE AIR AND DETERMINED THE SMELL WAS NOT COMING FROM ANY OF THE ENVIRONMENTAL SYSTEMS. WE DECIDED TO STAY WITH THE OUTSIDE AIR VENT SYSTEM AS THE SMELL STARTED TO GO AWAY. AFTER 10-15 MINUTES THE SMELL HAD COMPLETELY GONE AWAY AND CONTINUED THE FLIGHT. AFTER WE LANDED AT THE RIG, REFUELED AND LOADED FOR THE INBOUND FLIGHT, THE CONTROL ROOM RADIOED THAT THE OIM (WHO WAS ONBOARD) REPORTED SMELLING FUEL AND ALSO THAT A PASSENGER'S BAG SMELLED OF FUEL. I HAD THE OUTSIDE PILOT DO A SECOND THOROUGH WALKAROUND AND HE AGAIN DID NOT SEE ANY SIGNS OF FUEL ON/FROM THE AIRCRAFT OR IN THE BAGGAGE COMPARTMENT. HE ALSO REOPENED THE BAGGAGE COMPARTMENT AND DID NOT SMELL FUEL IN THAT AREA.  THE RETURN FLIGHT BACK WAS NORMAL WITH NO SIGNS OR SMELLS OF FUEL. AFTER SHUTDOWN WE CHECKED THE BAGGAGE COMPARTMENT AND THERE WERE NO SIGNS OR SMELL OF FUEL FROM THE RETURN FLIGHT. THIS WAS THE FIRST FLIGHT OF THE DAY FOR THIS AIRCRAFT. THE AIRCRAFT WAS PRESSURE REFUELED TO 4700LBS (4950 IS TOPPED OFF FOR THIS AIRCRAFT). THE PREVIOUS DAY THE AIRCRAFT WAS FULLY TOPPED OFF AND THIS DID NOT OCCUR. I HAVE BEEN FLYING THIS AIRCRAFT DAILY AND THIS IS THE FIRST TIME THIS OCCURRENCE. I ENTERED A DISCREPANCY IN RAMCO FOR MAINTENANCE TO FURTHER INVESTIGATE. ON 12/25/25, WE HAD AN INFLIGHT EMERGENCY DECLARED BY THE FLIGHT CREW FOR #1 ENGINE PROP SPEED ERRATIC. THE CREW REPORTED THE #1 ENGINE PROPELLER SPEED WAS JUMPING AROUND BETWEEN 1400 AND 1900 IN CLIMB SHORTLY AFTER TAKEOFF. THE CREW SAID ALL OTHER ENGINE INDICATIONS WERE NORMAL AND THE AIRCRAFT WAS NOT EXPERIENCING ANY ABNORMAL SOUNDS OR DIRECTIONAL CHANGES. HOWEVER, THEY DECLARED AN EMERGENCY AND LANDED WITHOUT INCIDENT SHORTLY THEREAFTER. 
WE FOUND THE #1 ENGINE PROPELLER TACH GENERATOR HOUSING LOOSE. THE SAFETY WIRE ON THE 4 SCREWS WAS PRESENT AND APPEARED UNDAMAGED BUT THE SCREWS WERE LOOSE AND THE HOUSING WAS LOOSE. AFTER REMOVING THE TACH GENERATOR, THE TACH SHAFT FELT VERY WOBBLY AND WOULD NOT SPIN/TURN EASILY AS COMPARED TO A NEW UNIT. WE REPLACED THE TACH GENERATOR AND THAT SEEMED TO HAVE SOLVED THE ERRATIC INDICATION PROBLEM.

UPON RECEIPT, PHI CONDUCTED A BORESCOPE INSPECTION AND NOTED DAMAGE ON THE 1ST STAGE TURBINE WHEEL. THE 1ST STAGE TURBINE WHEEL, NOZZLE, & 2ND STAGE TURBINE NOZZLE WERE SUBMITTED TO THE MATERIALS LAB IN INDIANAPOLIS, IN FOR ANALYSIS.  THE PRIMARY FINDINGS OF THE METALLURGICAL INVESTIGATION.   A SINGLE FIRST STAGE TURBINE WHEEL AIRFOIL FRACTURED AND LIBERATED IN HIGH CYCLE FATIGUE (HCF).  A SPHERICAL GAS HOLE APPROXIMATELY 0.009 INCH IN DIAMETER OBSERVED AT THE ORIGIN AREA.  THE OVERALL COMPOSITION AND MICROSTRUCTURE OF THE FIRST STAGE TURBINE WHEEL MET THE COMPONENT DEFINITION REQUIREMENTS. OVERALL VIEWS OF THE FIRST STAGE TURBINE WHEEL IN THE AS-RECEIVED  CONDITION ARE SHOWN IN FIGURE 1 (LEFT). THE FRACTURED AIRFOIL IS LABELED AS NR 1. 30 AIRFOILS EXHIBITED DAMAGE ON THE TRAILING HALF OF THE AIRFOILS, CONSISTENT WITH SECONDARY DAMAGE THAT OCCURRED AFTER THE LIBERATION OF AIRFOIL #1. A DETAILED VIEW OF AIRFOIL SURFACE IS SHOWN IN FIGURE 1 (RIGHT), EXHIBITING RADIATING LINES AND BEACH MARKS CONSISTENT WITH FATIGUE PROGRESSION OUTWARD FROM THE FRACTURE ORIGIN (ORANGE BORDER, AT THE SUCTION SIDE CROWN ROOT AREA AS SHOWN IN THE BLACK ARROWS) THEN TRANSITIONS TO OVERLOAD, INDICATED BY THE YELLOW DASHED LINES. THE FRACTURE ORIGIN WAS VISUALLY CONSISTENT WITH HIGH CYCLE FATIGUE INITIATION.FIGURE 1, TURBINE WHEEL AS RECEIVED (LEFT). DETAILED VIEW OF AIRFOIL NR 1 FRACTURE SURFACE (RIGHT) JURISDICTION EXPORT CONTROL CLASSIFICATION (RATING) USE OR DISCLOSURE OF THIS DATA IS SUBJECT TO THE RESTRICTION ON THE FIRST PAGE OF THIS DOCUMENT. AIRFOIL #1 WAS EXTRACTED FROM THE WHEEL AND THE FRACTURE SURFACE SUBJECTED TO SCANNING ELECTRON MICROSCOPIC (SEM) EXAMINATION. DETAILED IMAGES OF THE ORIGIN AREA AND FATIGUE REGION ARE SHOWN IN FIGURE 2. THE ORANGE ARROWS INDICATE DIRECTION OF FATIGUE PROGRESSION; THE DASHED YELLOW BORDER INDICATES THE FATIGUE FACETS. THE SOLID YELLOW BORDER INDICATES THE GAS HOLE AT THE ORIGIN. A PORE CONSISTENT WITH A GAS HOLE WAS LOCATED AT THE FATIGUE ORIGIN. THE GAS HOLE WAS APPROXIMATELY 0.009 INCH IN DIAMETER AND LOCATED APPROXIMATELY 0.009 INCHES FROM THE SUCTION SIDE OF THE AIRFOIL. FIGURE 2: DETAILED SEM IMAGES, ORIGIN LOCATION CONCLUSION BASED ON COMPREHENSIVE LABORATORY ANALYSIS, IT IS CONCLUDED THAT THE MOST PROBABLE CAUSE OF THE BLADE LIBERATION WAS THE PRESENCE OF A SPHERICAL GAS PORE LOCATED IN THE CROWN ROOT OF THE AIRFOIL. THIS SUBSURFACE GAS PORE SERVED AS THE INITIATION SITE FOR FATIGUE CRACKING, ULTIMATELY LEADING TO CRACK PROPAGATION AND OVERLOAD FRACTURE OF THE AFFECTED AIRFOIL.  THE M250 FAMILY OF STAGE 1 TURBINE BLISKS, INCLUDING THE SUBJECT PART (PN M250-10226), ARE MANUFACTURED USING A CENTER-OUTWARD CASTING PROCESS. THIS METHOD IS CONSISTENT WITH AEROSPACE INDUSTRY STANDARDS & IS SPECIFICALLY DESIGNED TO DRIVE RESIDUAL CONTAMINANTS AND CASTING ANOMALIES TOWARD THE OUTER DIAMETER,  THEREBY MINIMIZING THE RISK OF SUCH DEFECTS IN CRITICAL BORE REGIONS. A THOROUGH REVIEW OF THE FIXED MANUFACTURING PROCESS REVEALED NO SYSTEMATIC ISSUES. ALL PARTS UNDERGO RIGOROUS VISUAL, DIMENSIONAL,  FLUORESCENT PENETRANT, AND X-RAY INSPECTIONS. ADDITIONALLY, A LEVEL III NDT-CERTIFIED SPECIALIST IS CURRENTLY RE-EXAMINING THE HISTORICAL X-RAY RECORDS FOR THIS COMPONENT AT THE CASTING FACILITY.  A REVIEW OF HISTORICAL DATA FOUND NO EVIDENCE OF SIMILAR OCCURRENCES IN STAGE 1 BLISKS. GIVEN THAT THE GAS PORE IS ASSESSED TO BE AN ISOLATED, RANDOM ANOMALY, NO FLEETWIDE ACTIONS ARE RECOMMENDED AT THIS TIME.

DURING DESCENT FROM BIG BEAR, THE GARMIN AUTOPILOT ABRUPTLY DISCONNECTED FOLLOWING FAILURE OF THE GSA 28 PITCH SERVO. IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FAILURE, I OBSERVED A MOMENTARY PITCH-TRIM-DOWN INDICATION. THE AIRCRAFT USES MANUAL PITCH TRIM. UPON SERVO/AUTOPILOT DISCONNECT, THE AIRCRAFT PITCHED UP AGGRESSIVELY AND AIRSPEED DECAYED RAPIDLY. IMMEDIATE AND SUBSTANTIAL FORWARD CONTROL INPUT WAS REQUIRED TO LOWER THE NOSE, RECOVER AIRSPEED, AND MAINTAIN AIRCRAFT CONTROL. THE FAILED GSA 28 WAS WITHIN THE POPULATION IDENTIFIED BY GARMIN IN A SERVICE BULLETIN ADDRESSING POTENTIAL SERVO FAILURES. REPLACEMENT WAS RECOMMENDED BUT NOT MANDATORY. REPLACEMENT ULTIMATELY COST APPROXIMATELY $2,500. I AM CONCERNED THAT THE FINANCIAL AND LABOR BURDEN ASSOCIATED WITH CORRECTING A KNOWN SAFETY-RELATED FAILURE MODE MAY DISCOURAGE COMPLIANCE WITH A VOLUNTARY SERVICE BULLETIN, LEAVING AFFECTED SERVOS IN SERVICE UNTIL FAILURE.     GIVEN THE SIGNIFICANT FLIGHT-CONTROL UPSET RESULTING FROM THIS FAILURE, I RECOMMEND FAA REVIEW OF WHETHER VOLUNTARY CORRECTIVE ACTION PROVIDES ADEQUATE MITIGATION OR WHETHER MANDATORY CORRECTIVE ACTION IS WARRANTED.
